subject: SLA template: regional uptime parity & interim credit proposal
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@farsight.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@farsight.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on SLA regional parity & interim credits

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile. A quick follow-up from procurement: our platform rollout in EU will start next month and we need the SLA to guarantee parity between US and EU regions during the migration window.

Two specific asks:
- Can Redwood commit to the same uptime % for EU nodes as US (we currently see 99.9% in US) or provide an interim exception with commensurate credits while we validate EU performance?
- If an exception is required, can you outline a monthly credit mechanism (capped) we can use in contracts?

We're trying to avoid a long legal redline; if you can send a short proposal we can route it through procurement.

Appreciate it —
Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Cloud Ops, Farsight AI

--
Attachment: deployment_plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf, referenced)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@farsight.ai>
Cc: procurement@farsight.ai, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on SLA regional parity & interim credits

Nora —

Thanks for the clear asks. I attached our current SLA template (Redwood_SLA_Template_v3.docx) and a recent telemetry snapshot for the US fleet for context. Short answers up front: we aim for parity but we sometimes require a short onboarding period for new regions; when that happens we offer a temporary credit mechanism rather than permanently lowering the SLA.

Before I put formal language in a paper amendment, I've looped in Laura (legal), Marissa (sales ops) and Ben (finance) to scope an interim credit approach that:
- preserves our baseline guarantees where reasonable,
- caps customer exposure, and
- provides a clear sunset for the exception.

Could you confirm: 1) the expected go-live date for EU traffic, and 2) an estimated monthly spend for the next two months so we can size the credit cap?

I'll aim to follow up with a one-page proposal by end of day tomorrow.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Global Sales – Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Template_v3.docx (docx), uptime_telemetry_snapshot.csv (csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on SLA regional parity & interim credits (internal)

Sergio / team —

Quick legal notes for the proposed exception:
- If we provide a temporary region exception, we should keep the contractual uptime target language unchanged (do not lower the baseline). Instead, attach a temporary addendum titled "Regional Onboarding Credit (RO-Credit)".
- RO-Credit mechanics (suggested): prorated monthly credit based on percentage of affected requests to the EU region; cap the credit at 15% of the monthly invoice for up to two months.
- Limit exposure: explicitly exclude incidents caused by customer-configured network changes or third-party clouds.
- Sunset: automatic expiry after the second full billing period following EU go-live unless both parties agree to extend in writing.
- Auditability: require Redwood to provide uptime telemetry for the affected region and agree on a mutually acceptable metric (p95 request success and region-level availability).

I can draft the legal paragraph for the addendum; Marissa/Ben — please confirm the operational metrics and cap figure that makes sense from your side.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on SLA regional parity & interim credits (ops input)

Following up with operational suggestions:

- Baseline: propose we keep contract baseline at 99.9% (US) and offer an RO-Credit while EU is in the <12-week onboarding window.
- Credit calculation: simplest and defensible is a flat percentage of the monthly invoice for affected months — recommend 10% per month, with a cumulative cap equal to 20% (i.e., two months at 10% each). This keeps calculations easy for procurement and the customer.
- Measurement: we'll provide the region-level availability number from our monitoring (daily samples) and an accompanying CSV export; see attached sample: uptime_telemetry_snapshot.csv.
- Exceptions: maintenance windows we pre-announce will not trigger credits; unannounced third-party cloud outages will be excluded.

Operational ask: Sergio — if Farsight expects >$150k/mo in committed spend during the ramp, we could consider a modest increase in the cap (15%/month up to 30%) — finance to confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: uptime_telemetry_snapshot.csv (csv)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@farsight.ai>, procurement@farsight.ai
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on SLA regional parity & interim credits — proposed approach

Nora / procurement team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. After internal review, here's a concise proposal you can take to your legal team:

1) Regional baseline: Redwood will maintain the standard uptime baseline in the contract (99.9% as currently stated).

2) Regional Onboarding Credit (RO-Credit): For the first two full billing periods after EU go-live, Redwood will apply a monthly RO-Credit equal to 10% of the monthly invoice for months in which region-level availability for EU falls below 99.9%, capped at two months (total cap 20% of two months' invoice). RO-Credit will not apply to pre-announced maintenance or third-party cloud outages.

3) Auditability & Metrics: Redwood will provide daily region-level availability exports and a consolidated CSV for the billing period. Both parties agree to use p95 success + region availability as the measurement.

4) Sunset & Extension: RO-Credit auto-expires after two billing periods; extension only by written agreement.

5) Optional uplift: If Farsight commits to >=$150k/mo in reserved capacity during the onboarding window, Redwood will raise the monthly RO-Credit cap to 15% (two-month cumulative cap 30%).

Action items:
- Nora: confirm EU go-live date and estimated monthly spend so we can populate the addendum.
- Procurement: if acceptable, we will push the one-page addendum and a DocuSign link: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/FS-2026-09-029

If you'd like a track-changes word doc, Laura will add the legal paragraph and we can send a finalized addendum in the next 24 hours.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Global Sales — Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
